# `Scanner/FoldAway-v0` · A small field of view whose wrap-around misses the region

**B · Spatial encoding and reconstruction** · coverage of k-space · kind 2, set · isolates B15: Rectangular field of view and phase oversampling. [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** CANDIDATE: the gate has not been run (no stored result)

An object larger than the field of view folds over. The examination needs four regions free of wrap-around and does not care where else the image folds. The agent looks (a localiser costs scan time), finds where the object ends on the lines through each region, and prescribes the smallest phase field of view whose copies of the object miss the region. A field of view that holds the whole object is valid and too slow.

Kind of task: **undetermined** (no stored gate result).


| Given | Deliver | Scored by |
|---|---|---|
| A homogeneous object of hidden size, position and orientation; four marked regions inside it; the scanner; 30 s of scan time for looking | Per region, the geometry of a spin-echo scan: phase-encode axis, phase field of view, centre (level 3: rotation) | Re-scan on the hidden object against a twin without wrap-around: no aliased signal on the region, the region inside the image, scan time within 10 % of the fastest such geometry |

## World

- On the table: QA phantom (a homogeneous elliptical disc of gel), 1.5 T
- Sequences that matter here: spgr, se
- Formulas the agent is given: lines = matrix x phase_fov; scan time = overhead + TR x (1 + lines); a phase field of view of L repeats the object every L along the phase-encode axis: the region (r_lo, r_hi) is free of the copies of an object (o_lo, o_hi) when L > r_hi - o_lo and L > o_hi - r_lo; the readout does not wrap

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| size, position and orientation of the object | the target sequence with its readout field of view and matrix |
| its material | the four regions |
| fields and system state | the pass rule and its time factor |
| noise level | the instrument datasheet |
| the 128-bit world seed | realised protocol, timing, limits and cost of every plan and scan |
|  | any stored image, and the numbers along any line through it (the edges of the object have to be read from them) |

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'<region id>': {'pe_dir': 'y | x', 'phase_fov': '<fraction>', 'centre_y_mm': '<mm>', 'centre_x_mm': '<mm>', 'rotation_deg': '<degrees, level 3 only>'}}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan; the console accepts each geometry; the region lies inside the image; largest difference of a pixel of the region between the noise-free re-scan and its twin without wrap-around <= 0.05 of the region's mean; scan time <= 1.1 x the scan time of the fastest geometry that passes the gates above (search on the hidden world)
- Error: `largest over the regions of T / T_opt - 1: scan time of the delivered geometry over the oracle's optimum`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates, for every region

## Gate: the control policies on fresh instances

**Gate not stored on this engine** (`mrgym-engine-0.3.0`). `mrgym gate Scanner/FoldAway-v0 --n 300 --write` measures and stores it.

| Policy | Must | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `reference` | pass | one localiser; per region the ends of the object on the lines through it; fold-free phase field of view plus 2 pixels, along the better direction |
| `prior` | fail | no scan; the full phase field of view, centred on each region |
| `fixed_recipe` | fail | one token scan, then one geometry from the task text alone (axis and lines), tuned on other worlds |
| `whole_object` | fail | the NoWrap answer: the phase field of view holds the whole object along its narrowest direction |
| `region_only` | fail | one token scan, then the smallest phase field of view of the console, centred on the region |
| `sweep` | fail | one full scan and one small-field-of-view probe per region; keeps the small one where the region's signal did not change |
| `wrong_units` | fail | the reference's geometry with the phase field of view in millimetres |
| `fixed_axis` | ablation | the reference with the phase-encode axis always along y, never turned |
| `whole_extent` | ablation | the reference with the ends of the whole object instead of its ends on the lines through the region |
| `no_turn` | ablation | the reference with the better of the two upright axes, never turned |
| `no_margin` | ablation | the reference without the pixels kept for the ringing of the folded edge |
| `stated_method` | reported | the method level 1 states: one fold-free extent per region from the outermost ends of the object over its width, plus 2 pixels |
| `open_loop` | reported | a fixed scan list and a fixed estimator: the reference itself (no scan depends on a measurement) |

~~~text
# Prescribe the fastest scan in which no wrap-around lands on the marked region
A homogeneous test object lies in the scanner. It is larger than the field of view the examination can afford.
The long axis of the object lies along x or along y.
Four regions inside it are examined, each with its own spin-echo scan:
    sequence se, tr_ms 500, te_ms at the console minimum, bandwidth_hz_per_px 300, fov_mm 192, matrix 192
    (pixel 1 mm), 1 average, slice 5 mm, all of k-space sampled, no phase oversampling, not rotated.
Regions (circles; centre and radius in mm from the isocentre):
  A: y -6.5, x 38.3, radius 5
  B: y 31.7, x 31.4, radius 5
  C: y 15.7, x 10.4, radius 5
  D: y -27.8, x -41.6, radius 5
Deliver one geometry per region (A, B, C, D) with `submit`: the phase-encode axis (`pe_dir`), `phase_fov` (the phase field
of view as a fraction of fov_mm; the scan has 192 x phase_fov phase-encode lines), the centre of the field of view
(`centre_y_mm`, `centre_x_mm`, in mm from the isocentre).
Wrap-around is allowed anywhere except on the region. The target scans are not run in this episode: the scanner
evaluates the geometries you deliver.
Your own scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; only the deliverable is evaluated, on the scan the task names.
That scan is not charged to the scan-time budget and not limited by it.
Where the object ends is not known in advance.

Passing, for each region, on the scan with the geometry you delivered for it:
  the region lies inside the image;
  no aliased signal lands on the region: every pixel of the region differs by at most 5 % of the region's mean
  signal from the same pixel of the same scan without wrap-around;
  the scan takes at most 10 % longer than the fastest geometry that meets the two requirements above.
The scanner's log must show that you measured. A length in the wrong unit is wrong.

Limits. Scan time: 30 s (only `scan` spends it). Tool calls: 40 (every call counts once unless rejected). Rejected calls: 8 (a call refused for how it is written: unknown name, wrong type; costs nothing else), of them at most 3 refused `submit` calls. The episode ends at `submit` or at a limit; without `submit` the score is 0.
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier's re-scan and its twin are noise-free.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
